paragraphs.title: A World Full of Injustice and Suffering

easy.explanation: He saw “the tears of such as were oppressed.”
easy.q: What did Kohelet see among those who were oppressed?

easy.explanation: The passage twice says that they had no comforter.
easy.q: Did the oppressed have a comforter?

easy.explanation: He praised “the dead which are already dead” more than the living.
easy.q: Whom did Kohelet praise more than the living?

answers: The dead no longer see the evil under the sun
The dead can comfort the oppressed
medium.explanation: The living are still present in a world where evil is done under the sun.
medium.q: Why did Kohelet praise the dead more than the living?

answers: One who has not yet been
medium.explanation: The one who has not yet been has not seen the evil work done under the sun.
medium.q: Who does Kohelet say is better than both the dead and the living?

medium.explanation: The oppressed are those harmed by the power of their oppressors.
medium.q: What does “oppressed” mean in this passage?

answers: The living are better than the dead
The dead are better than the living, and the unborn are better than both
All three are presented as equal
challenge.explanation: The verses present a progression based on exposure to suffering and evil.
challenge.q: What order of preference does Kohelet present?

answers: They have no comforter, while their oppressors have power
They cannot see what is happening
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes both their lack of comfort and the power of their oppressors.
challenge.q: What especially strengthens the oppressed people’s sense of helplessness?

answers: To consider the evil work done under the sun
challenge.explanation: The comparison arises from Kohelet’s observation of suffering and evil in the world.
challenge.q: What is the main reason for comparing the living, the dead, and the unborn?

paragraphs.title: Labor, Envy, and the Value of Peace

easy.explanation: The passage says that a man is envied by his neighbour for his labor and right work.
easy.q: What may labor and a right work provoke?

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “The fool foldeth his hands together.”
easy.q: What does the fool do in verse 5?

easy.explanation: An handful with quietness is better than both hands full of travail and vexation.
easy.q: What does Kohelet say is better?

answers: The fool is idle, while labor may be accompanied by envy
The fool is rich, while the laborer is always peaceful
The fool is generous, while the laborer does not work
medium.explanation: The verses describe both harmful idleness and labor connected with envy.
medium.q: What contrast appears between the fool and the laboring person?

answers: His labor has no end and his eye is not satisfied with riches
medium.explanation: He keeps working and accumulating, yet his eye is not satisfied and he has no one with whom to share.
medium.q: Why does the solitary person continue to labor without enjoying his wealth properly?

medium.explanation: Quietness means peace or calm, in contrast with travail and vexation.
medium.q: What does “quietness” mean in “an handful with quietness”?

answers: He gathers riches without anyone to share their benefits with
He gives all his riches to others
challenge.explanation: He asks, “For whom do I labour, and bereave my soul of good?”
challenge.q: What criticism is made of the solitary person’s accumulation of wealth?

answers: As something that may be connected with envy and vexation
As something unrelated to other people
challenge.explanation: Labor and right work are discussed alongside envy, vanity, and vexation of spirit.
challenge.q: How is labor described in this passage?

answers: Folding the hands is harmful idleness, while quietness is peaceful contentment
challenge.explanation: Kohelet does not praise complete idleness; he prefers peaceful contentment to empty, excessive labor.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between folding the hands and choosing quietness?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “Two are better than one.”
One can lift up his fellow when he falls.
easy.q: What can one person do for his companion when he falls?

answers: A cord of two strands only
easy.explanation: The passage says, “a threefold cord is not quickly broken.”
easy.q: What is described as especially strong?

answers: A good reward for their labor
medium.explanation: The verse says that two have “a good reward for their labour.”
medium.q: What reward do two people working together have?

answers: Falling, cold, and resisting an attacker
medium.explanation: The examples include lifting one another, sharing warmth, and standing together against an attacker.
medium.q: In what situations is partnership useful according to these verses?

medium.explanation: It means helping a companion who has fallen.
medium.q: What does “lift up his fellow” mean in context?

answers: From isolation to mutual benefit and strength
challenge.explanation: The verses emphasize the advantages of companionship over being alone.
challenge.q: What is the main movement of thought in these verses?

answers: It emphasizes a bond that is difficult to break
It symbolizes a person working alone
challenge.explanation: The threefold cord represents unusual strength and unity.
challenge.q: Why does the image of a threefold cord fit the idea of partnership?

answers: Relationships provide help and protection in different situations
A person alone always succeeds more
challenge.explanation: Falling, cold, and attack all demonstrate the value of mutual help.
challenge.q: What conclusion is supported by all the examples in these verses?

easy.explanation: The passage compares a poor and wise child with an old and foolish king.
easy.q: Who may be better than an old and foolish king?

easy.explanation: The king “will no more be admonished,” meaning he is no longer willing to receive correction.
easy.q: What quality does the old king lack?

easy.explanation: The child is explicitly described as poor and wise.
easy.q: What was the condition of the child?

answers: Age and status matter more than wisdom
Wisdom may be better than wealth and status
medium.explanation: The wise child is preferred despite being poor, while the king lacks wisdom and teachability.
medium.q: What does the comparison between the child and the king teach?

answers: Good leadership requires teachability and sound judgment
medium.explanation: The passage shows that status alone does not guarantee capable leadership.
medium.q: How is the relationship between wisdom and leadership presented?

medium.explanation: To be admonished is to receive correction or wise instruction.
medium.q: What does “admonished” mean in this context?

answers: Status does not guarantee wisdom or leadership ability
challenge.explanation: The king has status but is described as old, foolish, and unwilling to receive correction.
challenge.q: What is the main criticism of relying on status alone?

answers: A poor and wise child versus an old and foolish king
challenge.explanation: The contrast between poverty, wisdom, age, and royal status sharpens the lesson.
challenge.q: What contrast builds the message of these verses?

answers: A person’s former condition does not guarantee the quality of his rule
The child cannot change his condition
challenge.explanation: The verse mentions the king’s rise from prison, but the larger point is that position and origin do not guarantee wise leadership.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the fact that the king came out of prison to reign?

paragraphs.title: The Hopes of Generations and Their Futility

easy.explanation: He saw them with “the second child that shall stand up in his stead.”
easy.q: With whom did Kohelet see all the living who walk under the sun?

answers: They do not rejoice in him
easy.explanation: The passage says that those who come after “shall not rejoice in him.”
easy.q: What do those who come after do regarding the new ruler?

answers: As vanity and vexation of spirit
easy.explanation: The passage concludes, “Surely this also is vanity and vexation of spirit.”
easy.q: How does Kohelet summarize this process?

answers: The next generation that replaces the previous one
medium.explanation: The second child represents the next ruler or generation who stands in the former ruler’s place.
medium.q: In whom do people place their hopes?

answers: Those who come after do not rejoice in the one who came before
medium.explanation: The text explicitly says that those who come after shall not rejoice in him.
medium.q: Why does the succession of generations fail to guarantee joy?

answers: The next generation replacing the previous one
Simply another child in a family
medium.explanation: The second child represents a successor who stands in the place of the former ruler.
medium.q: What does “the second child” represent in this idea?

answers: A new generation brings hope and replaces the former one, but it also fails to guarantee joy
Each generation succeeds more than the last
The older generation always remains in power
challenge.explanation: The succession of generations does not remove the vanity and dissatisfaction observed by Kohelet.
challenge.q: What repeated pattern is described in these verses?

answers: Hope for replacement and improvement does not guarantee a joyful result
Vanity comes only from refusing to work
challenge.explanation: Even the expectation placed in a successor may prove empty and disappointing.
challenge.q: What is the connection between hope in the next generation and vanity?

answers: It presents an unending succession of people and generations
It reduces the number of people
It describes the loneliness of one person
challenge.explanation: The expression emphasizes the continuing stream of generations and the repeated nature of the process.
challenge.q: Why does “there is no end of all the people” strengthen the message?

paragraphs.title: Entering the House of God and Listening

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God.”
easy.q: What should a person entering the house of God take heed to do?

easy.explanation: The verse says to be “ready to hear.”
easy.q: What should a person be ready to do in the house of God?

answers: It is offered without proper understanding
easy.explanation: The verse says that fools do not know that they do evil.
easy.q: What characterizes the sacrifice of fools?

medium.explanation: The verse joins keeping one’s foot with being ready to hear.
medium.q: What is the proper attitude toward the house of God according to the verse?

medium.explanation: The verse emphasizes hearing rather than performing a foolish act without understanding.
medium.q: What is presented as better than the sacrifice of fools?

medium.explanation: The expression describes attentive and serious listening.
medium.q: What does “ready to hear” mean in this context?

answers: A religious act without understanding is not an expression of wisdom
Every sacrifice is better than listening
Listening has no connection with the house of God
challenge.explanation: The verse criticizes the sacrifice of fools because they do not understand that they are doing evil.
challenge.q: What does the contrast between hearing and sacrifice teach?

answers: Entering requires preparation and care, not careless action
It commands people to run to the house of God
challenge.explanation: Keeping one’s foot suggests a careful and reverent approach.
challenge.q: How does “keep thy foot” connect with the idea of listening?

answers: The problem is not only the sacrifice but their failure to understand their conduct
Fools never enter the house of God
challenge.explanation: The verse identifies their lack of understanding: they do not know that they do evil.
challenge.q: What detail about fools is easy to overlook?
